clue.text: What bad driver may have to do after accident with cute peewit

definitions.text: What bad driver may have to do

indicators.note: an accident leaves things smashed and jumbled, so the letters of the following words are reordered

explanation.surface: A motorist has a crash involving a wading bird, the lapwing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a motorist but is a golf club; a poor drive off the tee may mean placing the ball again. The peewit is the lapwing.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer who drives badly may have to place the ball on its peg again, a second go at the start of the hole.

clue.text: International trial

definitions.meaning: an international cricket match between national sides is a ...
a trial is an examination of something's quality

explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international cricket fixture, and a trial is an examination or check.

clue.text: Say I start singing Elijah after end of Handel's lament

indicators.note: the preceding pieces are placed after the composer's ending in the answer

parts.note: the closing pair of letters of the composer's name
EG, short for exempli gratia, means 'say' as in 'for example'

indicators.note: the start of each of the words singing and Elijah supplies a letter

explanation.surface: A singer begins Handel's oratorio Elijah, reaching its final mournful number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of Handel's' here is its last two letters, EL; 'start' takes the first letters of 'singing' and 'Elijah'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament someone in verse is to write an elegy for them, a mournful poem.

clue.text: Where investor seeks company to tackle city hill

parts.note: a military company is made up largely of privates, the lowest-ranked soldiers
EC is the postcode for the City of London
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An investor hunts for a firm to take on a hill development in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' looks like part of the definition but supplies the soldiers; 'to tackle' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Businesses owned privately rather than by the state are where an investor looks to put money.

clue.text: Might as well report champagne stolen in Stepney

indicators.note: a report is something said aloud, so what is spoken stands for the entry

parts.note: champagne is a wine, and stolen goods are 'hot', which a Cockney in Stepney would say without its H

explanation.surface: Someone reports that bubbly has been nicked in an East End district.
explanation.walkthrough: Stepney is in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the H, so 'hot' becomes 'ot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an agreeing shrug, the same as saying there's no reason not to.

clue.text: Invitation to elope or separate

definitions.meaning: a lover's plea to run off together
as a verb, to come apart or become detached

explanation.definitionFit: A suitor urges a beloved to run off with them; a part that detaches from its fixing also comes loose this way.

clue.text: High rollers make site visits

definitions.meaning: big breaking waves rolling onto a beach
to browse from website to website on the internet

explanation.definitionFit: Breaking waves on a shore are surf, and browsing the web from page to page is surfing.

clue.text: Apparently more complete speaker

parts.note: utter means complete or absolute, as in utter nonsense
the comparative ending -er means more

explanation.surface: A speaker who seems even more thorough than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' admits the comparative is a made-up word: it only looks like 'more utter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who says words aloud is one who utters, a talker or speaker.

clue.text: Middle ranking new age fiddler

indicators.note: a new version of the following letters is a fresh arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A violinist of the New Age movement is only of medium standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Majors, lieutenant colonels and colonels hold this rank, in the middle between junior and general officers.

clue.text: Determine whether to follow City and watch outside

indicators.note: the watching word sits outside, around the other pieces

parts.note: to spy is to watch secretly

indicators.note: the word for whether comes after the City letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
if can mean whether, as in 'ask if he's coming'

explanation.surface: Deciding whether to support Manchester City and watch the match outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine details is to state them precisely, to set them out exactly.

clue.text: Hearing two insects is a possibility

indicators.note: what is heard is the spoken sound, not the spelling

parts.note: a mite and a bee, two small creepy-crawlies

explanation.surface: Hearing a pair of insects buzzing is a possibility.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly a mite is an arachnid, but crosswords commonly lump it with insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something could be so means it's possible, not certain.

clue.text: Magnificent gallery featuring Chair once

parts.note: grand means magnificent or splendid
the National Gallery in Trafalgar Square, London

explanation.surface: A splendid art gallery displays a chair from former times.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chair is the biggest fence of the Aintree steeplechase and, unlike most of its fences, is jumped only once in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Liverpool horse race is the event whose course includes the Chair fence, cleared a single time.

clue.text: Cocktail girl follows secure convention

indicators.note: the girl's name comes after the other pieces

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or secure
Acol is the standard bidding convention in British bridge
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl shows up after a conference has been booked.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum, coconut and pineapple drink is a well-known mixed drink served in bars.

clue.text: Bloody warfare destroys houses

indicators.note: the words house, or contain, the letters needed across their join

explanation.surface: Brutal fighting levels homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun for buildings destroyed but is a verb telling you the words contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bloody is covered in blood, which is crimson in colour.

clue.text: Expulsion by run down landlords before time

indicators.note: the pieces before come ahead of the time letter

parts.note: to dis is slang for to disparage or run down
pub landlords serve behind the bar, as barmen

explanation.surface: Pub landlords evicted before closing for running down their premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck off as a barrister is a formal expulsion from the legal profession.

clue.text: Girls regularly former partners of The Hollies

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one of the word Girls

parts.note: exes are former spouses or partners

explanation.surface: Female fans who were once partners of members of the 1960s pop band The Hollies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hollies were a British pop group; here the name is just the plural of holly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus of holly, so its plural names several holly trees.

clue.text: Gypsy starts winning with pair of queens

indicators.note: the start of the word winning gives its first letter

parts.note: and means with, joining two things

indicators.note: two copies of the royal abbreviation follow

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A traveller begins a card game holding two queens.
explanation.definitionFit: A gypsy traditionally has no fixed home and roams from place to place.

clue.text: Italian constituent's austerity Blair quoted

indicators.note: something quoted is repeated in speech, so how it sounds matters

parts.note: rigour means austerity or strictness, and Tony is the first name of former Prime Minister Blair

explanation.surface: An Italian voter repeats something about Tony Blair's austerity.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was UK Prime Minister 1997-2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbed pasta tubes are a staple ingredient of Italian cooking, hence a part of an Italian meal.

clue.text: Bad vibes about endless Benny Hill

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the trimmed name
bad means corrupted or out of order, so the letters of vibes are jumbled
with both ends gone, only the middle letters of Benny remain

explanation.surface: Bad vibes surround the late comedian Benny Hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges VIBES to BEVIS; ENN goes inside after its B. Benny Hill was a British TV comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's highest mountain is a peak in the Scottish Highlands, called a hill in Scots fashion.

clue.text: No-one asked Mandela if being independent advantaged leaders of country

indicators.note: the leading letters of each of the preceding words are taken

explanation.surface: Nobody asked Nelson Mandela whether independence favoured the nation's rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern African nation, neighbour of South Africa, independent since 1990.

clue.text: Happy chappy, happy to secure a happy ending

indicators.note: to secure is to hold inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: glad means happy

indicators.note: the ending of the word happy is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow is pleased to arrange a happy ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned phrase for a merry young fellow, a cheerful chap.

clue.text: It only gets slightly damaged alongside

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of order
only a slight part of the word gets is used, its first letter

explanation.surface: A thing only gets a bit damaged when placed next to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship lying-to sits stationary, hove to, which may be next to another vessel.

clue.text: Half wits add to speed king's disapproval

indicators.note: half of the word wits is taken, here its back half

parts.note: KTS, knots, is a measure of speed at sea
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch frowns at fools who boost a vehicle's speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The clicking sound made with the tongue expresses mild reproach or disapproval.

clue.text: 24 of West Indian cricketers?

parts.note: 24 is the solution meaning morale of a side; read as the spirit drunk in the Caribbean it is a cane liquor

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 24-across, whose second word is also a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribbean cane liquor is the classic West Indian spirit, so it is a West Indies team's spirit.

clue.text: Passion for side order is part time

indicators.note: putting the following letters in order rearranges them

explanation.surface: Keen on a side dish, but only part-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side order' looks like a dish; 'side' belongs to the definition and 'order' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty and enthusiasm a player feels for the team is morale or camaraderie.

clue.text: Overwhelm insane uprising

indicators.note: in a down light the word rises, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nuts is slang for insane

explanation.surface: A mad revolt crushes all before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or overwhelm, as with shock or a blow.

clue.text: Thus maintaining degree of restraint

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, thus
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: So it keeps a measure of self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A ban on trade with a country is an official restriction or restraint.

clue.text: Child keeps close after dark

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the child word holds the other inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh means near or close

explanation.surface: A youngster stays near home once night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is the coming night, the time after dark today.

clue.text: Dealt with missing opener being out for a duck

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the word Dealt loses its first letter, its opening

explanation.surface: A batsman, his opening partner gone, is out for a duck, nought runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater dabbling bird is a kind of duck.

clue.text: Piece of America revolutionised in one click

indicators.note: revolutionised means completely changed, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A slice of the United States transformed with one mouse click.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-cent coin is a US piece of money, the word piece meaning a coin.
